decision: scoped this run to Phase 1 of the brief only
why: the brief says begin with Phase 1 and later phases depend on the CRDT core

decision: defined done as go test -race green plus live convergence of real WebSocket clients over real Postgres
why: a passing unit suite alone would not prove the services work together

decision: chose high rigor for the CRDT and its wire format
why: the ID ordering and snapshot format are hard to change once data is stored

decision: ran Postgres 17 in docker compose on port 55432 for integration tests
why: tests must hit a real database, not a mock

decision: asked two other models to sketch the design independently before coding
why: the RGA layout and GC rule are one-way doors worth designing twice

decision: switched the RGA from a linked list to a parent-pointer tree with ID-sorted children
why: the tree's text is fixed by the set of nodes, so replicas converge even with bad clocks; the list needed valid Lamport clocks to converge

decision: kept Lamport clocks over Grok's gapless per-client counters
why: with per-client counters a new insert can sort after older siblings and appear in the wrong place

decision: kept GC to tombstones with no children whose insert and delete are covered by the stable vector
why: both sketches showed that moving a tombstone's children to its parent reorders text

decision: made the op log idempotent with a unique key on each op ID
why: a retried append must not double count toward the 100-op snapshot cadence

decision: kept JSONB snapshots as the brief mandates despite Grok preferring bytea
why: the brief names JSONB explicitly; size cost goes to the user as an open decision
